name: The Wishing Garden
pitch: The child finds a tiny painted door in the garden wall and slips into a miniature world of tea-party flowers, kind little creatures and small, gentle magic.
setting: The Wishing Garden, a tiny secret world behind a painted door in an old garden wall: rose bushes as tall as houses, teacup ponds, toadstool cottages with lace curtains, ribbon-tied bluebell lanterns, strawberry patches, a wishing well made from a thimble, and a soft moonlit meadow for the Moon Picnic

supportingCast.name: Clementine
supportingCast.role: brave, warm-hearted friend who leads the way
supportingCast.look: a small cream bunny with pink-lined ears, a butter-yellow knitted cardigan with tiny heart buttons, and a daisy tucked behind one ear

supportingCast.name: Pipkin
supportingCast.role: tiny, thoughtful friend who notices small things
supportingCast.look: a little grey field mouse in a blush-pink pinafore with a thimble for a hat and a tiny woven basket

supportingCast.name: Luma
supportingCast.role: a shy little firefly who has lost her glow
supportingCast.look: a tiny round firefly with lacy pale-blue wings, rosy cheeks and a soft golden tail that has gone dim

storyBeats: a painted door in the garden wall
a little problem with a reason
a kind try that doesn't quite work
powerIdeas: The child's gentleness, kindness or way of noticing tiny things is what helps; one of the child's favorite things can become a small, magical detail of the garden.

artDirection.mood: whimsical, nostalgic and enchanted, sweet and delicate, glowing with childlike wonder and soft light

contentRules: gentle and cozy throughout; no villains, chases or scary moments
magic is small, kind and wondrous
friends help in small, practical ways

starters.title: Luma's Lost Glow
starters.summary: On the night of the Moon Picnic, a shy little firefly has lost her glow, and the lanterns can't be lit without her.
starters.idea: Luma the firefly has lost her glow on the night of the Moon Picnic, and the lanterns can't be lit without her. A jar of moonlight and Clementine's brave pep talk don't work. Pipkin notices Luma glows when she feels loved, the child gives her a tiny daisy crown and a hug, and her glow lights every bluebell lantern.

starters.title: The Teacup Pond Party
starters.summary: The roses have planned a tea party, but the teacup pond has gone dry the very morning of the party.
starters.idea: The roses have planned a tea party but the teacup pond has gone dry. Carrying water in thimbles is too slow and a raincloud won't come. The child spots a sleepy snail sitting on the little spring, kindly helps him move, and the pond fills just in time for a sparkling tea.

starters.title: The Sleepy Sunflower Clock
starters.summary: The tall sunflower that wakes the garden each morning won't wake up, and the Morning Parade can't begin.
starters.idea: The garden wakes when the tall Sunflower Clock turns its face to the sun, but today it slept through sunrise behind a thick morning mist, so the Morning Parade can't start. Ringing the bluebells only wakes the bees, and Pipkin's feather tickle makes it sneeze but not wake. The child remembers their shiny button (shown at the start) and holds it up to catch the first ray of light through the mist, shining it onto the sunflower's face. It stretches, turns, and the parade begins.

starters.title: The Moonlight Lullaby
starters.summary: The night breeze has lost its lullaby, and nobody in the Wishing Garden can fall asleep.
starters.idea: Every night the breeze hums a lullaby through the seashell chimes, but tonight the chimes are tangled and the garden can't fall asleep. Clementine hums loudly, but it's too bouncy to be sleepy, and counting stars makes everyone wide awake. The child gently untangles the chimes with Pipkin's help, then softly sings the bedtime song their own grown-up sings to them at home (set up at the start). The breeze learns it, and the whole garden drifts to sleep, and so does the child, back at home.

starters.title: Grandma Mouse's Birthday Basket
starters.summary: Pipkin has picked the perfect strawberries for his grandma's birthday, but his little basket is far too heavy to carry across the garden.
starters.idea: Pipkin wants to bring a basket of strawberries to Grandma Mouse's birthday across the garden, but it's too heavy for him. Clementine tries carrying it on her head and the strawberries tumble out. The child notices an empty walnut shell and four round buttons (from the child's coat, mentioned at the start), and together they build a tiny wagon. They pull it past the rose bushes and over the moss bridge, and arrive just as Grandma Mouse lights her candle.

starters.title: The Rainbow Seed
starters.summary: The garden's rainbow seed won't sprout, and without it there will be no rainbow over the Wishing Garden this spring.
starters.idea: Each spring the garden plants one rainbow seed, and its flower paints the rainbow in the sky. This year it won't sprout. Watering it more just makes a muddy puddle, and Clementine's cheerful singing doesn't help. Pipkin notices the seed is in the cold shadow of a big leaf. The child gently moves the big leaf aside so the warm sun reaches the seed, and ties their favorite-colored ribbon to the stem so everyone remembers to give it sun. The flower opens, and a rainbow arcs over the garden.
